title: Staged archive-based restore and feedback-driven load-shedding playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce an operational playbook and validation harness for staged restores originating from cold/archive snapshots, coupled with a feedback-driven load-shedding and circuit-breaker calibration strategy for active->passive cutovers. The goal is to make scheduled failover drills reproducible, measurable against SLOs, and safe for user-facing traffic while minimizing data-rehydration latency and unexpected error budgets.

Scope:
- Restore path: archive snapshot (long-term cold storage) -> incremental rehydration of index/kv shards -> verification with hash-based snapshot compare.
- Traffic strategy: progressive traffic reintroduction with per-route priority bands, dynamic load-shedding triggered by real-time SLO signals, and adaptive circuit-breaker thresholds during the rehydration window.
- Validation: automated smoke suites, synthetic client traffic, and canary (1%-5%) split before full cutover.
- Observability: SLO dashboards, tail-latency percentiles, per-model token error rates, token-level cost spikes, and kv-compare integrity counters.

High-level runbook steps:
1) Pre-checks (T-minus 48h): verify latest cold snapshot indexed list, confirm signed checksums in archive, ensure recovery IAM roles and KMS keys available, freeze non-essential batch jobs that write to tokenstore.
2) Snapshot pull (T-minus 2h): restore minimal index headers first, compute partial checksums, and stage the archive blobs to local restore nodes (prefer local SSD cache).
3) Incremental rehydrate (T-minus 1h -> +2h): progressively hydrate hot shards prioritized by traffic heatmap (models/routes with highest QPS first). Track per-shard rehydrate ETA and backpressure signals.
4) KV/hash compare: run deterministic hash scans on restored key ranges and compare to archived checksums; allow a small drift window for transient in-flight writes (documented tolerance policy).
5) Canary traffic (Start): route 1% of production reads to restored passive region with synthetic probe agents verifying generation quality and latency; simultaneously enable fine-grained circuit breakers on the passive cluster.
6) Feedback-driven load-shedding: if observed latency or error budget usage exceeds configured thresholds, progressively shed lower-priority routes (batch embeddings, offline warming requests) using a priority table. Adjust shedding steps based on SLO breach severity.
7) Progressive promotion: after 60-minute stability window with green health checks and KV integrity within tolerance, ramp traffic in increments to 25%, 50%, then 100% with a canary pause at each step to re-evaluate SLOs.
8) Post-cutover validation: run full acceptance tests, reconcile transaction logs, and snapshot the newly promoted primary for archive continuity.
9) Rollback criteria: defined latency/EU thresholds, failed KV compare > tolerance, or an unrecoverable error in rehydration pipeline. Rollback plan: drain traffic from passive->active, reenable circuit-breaker hard-fail mode, and schedule forensic snapshot.

Instrumentation & metrics to collect during drill:
- per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, tail CPU/GPU utilization, token generation error-rate, token cost per request, circuit-breaker trip count, shard rehydrate progress, kv-compare mismatch count, archive transfer throughput.

Safety & trade-offs:
- Cold-archive restores reduce storage costs but increase rehydration latency; to mitigate we pre-stage critical index headers and use prioritized shard rehydration.
- Aggressive pre-warm increases cost but reduces failover time — trade-off will be parametrized by customer SLO tier and region.
- Load-shedding must be conservative for high-value routes; a prioritized mapping will be maintained in the runbook and automatically enforced by routing policy.

Deliverables:
- This runbook (operationalized checklists and playbook steps).
- Automated validation harness (kitchen-sink synthetic traffic + kv-compare runner).
- Dashboard: drill-run summary with pre/post SLO comparisons and artifact links.
- Post-drill report template and action-item tracker.

Acceptance criteria:
- Drill completes full restore and promotion in the scheduled window at least twice in staging without exceeding predefined SLO breach budget.
- KV/hash compare shows mismatches <= documented tolerance.
- Load-shedding policy executed and correctly prioritized routes dropped in test scenarios.
- Playbook reviewed and signed off by SRE, Platform, and Security leads.
checklist: Confirm archive checkpoint and checksum signed in object store
Allocate restore nodes and SSD cache reservation
Pre-suspend non-critical write jobs and analytics exports
Execute preflight synthetic probes against passive region
Start archive pull and verify partial headers
Run incremental rehydrate by priority bands
Run kv/hash compare and record mismatch metrics
Apply feedback-driven shedding if SLO signals degrade
Ramp traffic with pause windows and final acceptance tests
Snapshot post-promotion state and close drill runbook
